channel.title: Andrew Concepcion Blog
channel.description: Engineering logs, essays, and field notes by Andrew Concepcion.

item.title: It’s Not Okay to Not Be Okay
item.description: We have become fluent in naming what hurts. But awareness can become another form of avoidance when it never turns into care, accountability, or action.

item.title: The Fortress We Mistake for Home
item.description: A reflection on the defenses we build from old wounds, pride, and habit—and why real change begins when we stop guarding what keeps us trapped.

item.title: What Building a Small Backend Taught Me About AI-Ready Engineering
item.description: Lessons from a compact backend: explicit API contracts, append-only location history, PostGIS semantics, guarded AI prose, and evidence-based verification.

item.title: Agents That Leave Receipts
item.description: A practical reflection on local agents, memory, verification, and the handoffs that let the next run trust what happened.

item.title: How I Use MemPalace to Make Local Agents Better
item.description: How I set up MemPalace as a practical tool for local agents: small taxonomy, verify-first retrieval, agent diaries, AAAK wake-up context, and why protocol matters more than storage.

item.title: Deep Dive: One Rust Core Across Android and iOS
item.description: How a Rust facade, UniFFI bindings, and platform packaging can give Android and iOS one domain core without duplicating behavior.

item.title: Career Growth as Ownership, Not Just Job Titles
item.description: A practical framework for reading engineering growth through scope, decision quality, operational responsibility, and durable outcomes.

item.title: Using Emergenetics and Harrison as Calibration Tools
item.description: How I use two assessment profiles as prompts for better decisions and communication—without treating their scores as identity or proof of ability.

item.title: End-to-End and Visual QA for Personal Websites
item.description: A practical quality loop for static personal sites: verify the publication boundary, exercise critical routes, and review desktop and mobile rendering.

item.title: Building an Editable Blog That Still Works on GitHub Pages
item.description: How SQLite authoring, deterministic static generation, and a public-only build artifact create an editable blog without shipping a runtime database.

item.title: From Mobile Developer to AI-Accelerated Engineer
item.description: How agentic tools widened my engineering workflow without replacing mobile depth, explicit ownership, or evidence-based delivery.

item.title: Prompt Patterns for Reviewable, Production-Ready Code
item.description: A practical prompt structure for coding agents: live context, real constraints, side-effect boundaries, observable acceptance evidence, and reproducible handoffs.

item.title: Running an Agent Fleet Without Losing the Plot
item.description: Lessons from multi-agent engineering work: define output contracts, instrument repeated effort, match verification to risk, and preserve trustworthy handoffs.

item.title: A Month in New Zealand
item.description: Family holidays in Auckland, a compressed South Island road trip, and the surprise of catching the Aurora Australis.

item.title: MySTC: Leading a Five-Person Android Team
item.description: I led five senior Android engineers on MySTC, working in Kotlin and Java across account, ordering, support, and multilingual flows.

item.title: Quiet Systems: Reflection Rituals for Builders
item.description: A personal essay about designing focus blocks, protecting rest, and keeping philosophy close to the shipping calendar.

item.title: OCBC Business: Android Banking Work
item.description: I worked on OCBC Business for Android in Kotlin and XML, covering chart UI, identity-verification integration, network behavior, and focused unit tests.

item.title: Weekend Photo Experiments: Paradise Mist, Dobsonian Moon, and Lake Pukaki
item.description: Three frames from one trip, one ongoing experiment: motion, moon detail, and mountain light across different gear and shooting constraints.

item.title: openpay: Checkout, Spend Limits, and Release Edges
item.description: I worked on openpay's Android purchase flow, including spend-limit cards, merchant content, checkout state, and partner-dependent payment paths.

item.title: Solo: Android Across a White-Label Food Platform
item.description: I worked in Solo's shared Kotlin and XML codebase, shipping Android features and production fixes used by multiple restaurant-branded apps.

item.title: OWTO: Android, iOS, and the Backend Between Them
item.description: I led delivery across OWTO's Android, iOS, and backend work and stayed hands-on with booking, GPS, payments, and the APIs connecting them.

item.title: Building Across Kotlin and Swift Without Blurring Platform Boundaries
item.description: A practical way to divide shared domain behavior, state, packaging, and native UI responsibilities across Kotlin and Swift.

item.title: Popslide: Experiments on a Lockscreen Product
item.description: I built and evaluated Android experiment variants for Popslide and worked on lockscreen behavior, notifications, caching, and production state handling.

item.title: WebSafety: Parental Controls Meet Platform Limits
item.description: I worked on WebSafety features across Java and Objective-C code, including GPS, synchronization, permissions, and platform behavior that wasn't always documented.

item.title: ProjectBASS: Crowdsourced Network Measurements
item.description: I contributed Kotlin feature and maintenance work to ProjectBASS, an open-source Android app for collecting volunteer network measurements.
